biography.plain_text: Patrick Heiniger was an Argentine-born Swiss lawyer and luxury-watch executive who led Rolex from 1992 to 2008. Following his father André at the company, he drove a sweeping vertical-integration programme, acquiring suppliers and consolidating production into four modern sites. He also established Rolex's Mentor and Protégé Arts Initiative to support emerging artists.

long_biography.plain_text:
Rolex's vertically integrated manufacture was the defining institutional achievement of Patrick Heiniger's tenure. Under his direction, the watchmaker brought component suppliers into the group and concentrated previously dispersed operations in four purpose-built Swiss sites. The reorganisation gave Rolex tighter control over quality and production while reinforcing its independence.

Heiniger came to that role with a substantial family advantage. Born in Buenos Aires to André and Odette Heiniger, he studied law in Geneva, trained further in New York and co-founded an international and intellectual-property practice. His father, then leading Rolex, recruited him to oversee marketing and sales. Heiniger succeeded André in 1992 as the third leader in the company's history. He stepped down in 2008 after sixteen years at the helm and died in Monte Carlo five years later.
